answer: A market pays agents to survey sparrow nests and ember damage in karst woodland. To claim a daily work slot, an operator proves possession of a valid government identity credential and reveals a market-and-day nullifier derived from its unique person identifier. The market rejects repeated nullifiers, so aliases backed by the same person cannot claim extra slots without exposing their identity. This requires an issuer that assigns one stable identifier per person; stolen credentials remain a risk.
